summary: A realistic IELTS listening test with long scripts and a clear trap on almost every question in Parts 1-3. No answer keys were wrong. Part 4's notes repeat the lecture closely, so it is a little easier than a real Part 4, and several paraphrase pairs were not real paraphrases and have been fixed or removed.
strengths: Part 1 (724 words) has corrections and distractors throughout: third/fourth floor, 5th/12th September, large/medium van, 800/700, bank transfer refused, boxes free but tape not.

Part 2 MCQs mention and reject two plausible options each; the matching box paraphrases well (former member of staff / worked in our shop for thirty years; recently returned from abroad / come home after two years on loan).
Part 3 (909 words) is a full academic planning discussion; the multi-select items reject three options each with reasons.
Answers appear in question order and gap answers are single, correctly spelled words.

issues.problem: Pair had the same words on both sides ('more importantly' / 'more importantly').
issues.change: Removed; no real paraphrase exists for this gap ('removed plants and, more importantly, skilled ____' repeats the lecture).

issues.problem: Pair's question side 'the marker will expect' is from the script, not the question.
issues.change: Pair now ['burn the dried sample', 'burning samples'].

issues.problem: Pair ['ten working days ahead', '10 working days ahead'] was a number format, not a paraphrase.
issues.change: Removed. Also tightened Q13 and Q20 and added 8 new pairs.

issues.problem: Part 4 notes 31, 32, 35, 38 and 40 copy the lecture's wording ('a single ____, Camellia sinensis'; 'made fashionable by a Portuguese ____'), so these items test word-catching more than understanding.
issues.change: Reword the stems in a future edit, e.g. 35 'Charles II's Portuguese wife, a ______, made tea popular at court'.

issues.problem: Q27 option B 'sieving and weighing dried samples' is said word for word.
